# Terrain Viewer

> Free, open-source web viewer for elevation data (DEM, DTM, DSM, LiDAR) by Iconem, built on MapLibre GL JS. It shows terrain in 2D, 3D and on a globe with hillshade, hypsometric tint, contours, slope, aspect, curvature, local relief model, sky-view factor, openness, matcap and Phong lighting, compares sources side by side, and exports GeoTIFFs. It reads global terrain (Mapterhorn, AWS, Mapbox, MapTiler) and national LiDAR and open-data services, COG, VRT, WMS, ArcGIS LERC and Cesium quantized mesh, all in the browser.

Every setting lives in the URL, so a link opens a place in a given mode. To send someone to a view, build a URL on https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/ with query parameters. The full list, with types and defaults, is the OpenAPI description at https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/openapi.json and the page https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/url-api/.

## Building a link

- Camera: `lat`, `lng`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`; `viewMode` is `2d`, `3d` or `globe`.
- Terrain source: `terrainSourceA`, for example `mapterhorn` (global, the default), `aws`, or a library id such as `custom-mx-aguadafenix-lidar`.
- Modes: `showHillshade`, `showColorRelief` (hypsometric tint), `showContoursAndGraticules` with `showContours`, `showTerrainAnalysis` with `showSlope`, `showAspect`, `showCurvature`, `showReliefVisualization` with `showLrm`, `showSvf`, `showOpenness`, `showLightingEffects` with `showMatcap`, `showPhong`, `showRasterBasemap`.
- Comparison: `splitStyle` (`side-by-side` or `overlay`) with `terrainSourceB`.

Examples:

- Slope around the Matterhorn in 3D: https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/?viewMode=3d&zoom=13&lat=45.9763&lng=7.6586&pitch=55&showTerrainAnalysis=true&showSlope=true
- Contours over a Maya LiDAR survey: https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/?viewMode=2d&zoom=15&lat=17.7338&lng=-91.2886&terrainSourceA=custom-mx-aguadafenix-lidar&showContoursAndGraticules=true&showContours=true&showHillshade=true
- Hillshade and sky-view factor anywhere: https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/?zoom=12&lat=<lat>&lng=<lng>&showHillshade=true&showReliefVisualization=true&showSvf=true

## Skill

Agents that support skills can install one that does this for them: `npx skills add Iconem/terrain-viewer` (source: https://github.com/Iconem/terrain-viewer/blob/main/skills/terrain-viewer/SKILL.md).

## Overview

- [Changelog](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/changelog/): What shipped, and when — the TL;DR of every release
- [Developer documentation](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/): How Terrain Viewer is built, for contributors and the curious. Setup and structure, the URL as an API, the custom tile protocols, the historical imagery adapters, and the internals of the map and the interface.
- [Features of Terrain Viewer: hillshade, slope, contours, 3D, historical imagery](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/): Every feature of the free browser terrain viewer, section by section: hillshade and lighting, slope and terrain analysis, contours, hypsometric tint, 3D and globe, split views, historical imagery, national LiDAR, your own COGs, export and share.
- [Terrain Viewer Overview: a free browser viewer for elevation data](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/overview/): What Terrain Viewer is (hillshade, slope, contours, 3D and historical imagery on global terrain, national LiDAR or your own GeoTIFF, with no install) and how its sidebar is organised.

## Developer documentation

- [Advocacy](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/advocacy/): Where Terrain Viewer has been presented, where it still could be, and the upstream threads it takes part in — venues per country for LiDAR and open elevation data
- [#30DayMapChallenge 2026: all 30 themes, with a map idea and a place for each](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/advocacy/map-challenge/): The 30 daily themes of the 2026 #30DayMapChallenge, each with a terrain or imagery map idea, a place to try it and the free browser tool that draws it: hillshade, contours, lidar, historical imagery, 3D
- [Post drafts](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/advocacy/post-drafts/): The announcement and showcase posts behind the Advocacy list, as Markdown ready to paste
- [Venues per country](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/advocacy/venues/): Where a release or showcase post fits, per national LiDAR and elevation dataset, plus the cross-cutting venues
- [Camera Sync](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/camera-sync/): Keeping up to eight map views on one camera — elevation as the sixth parameter, the idle settle, and the rules that keep gestures intact
- [GEM-15 and Open Buildings, cell-routed sources](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/cell-routed-sources/): gem15:// and openbuildings:// — two Google datasets served as thousands of per-cell COGs on Cloud Storage, read in the browser through the VRT reader with one VRT built per cell on the fly, and the JSON API media endpoint that makes the bucket readable at all
- [Change Detection Frameworks](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/change-detection-frameworks/): Labelling before/after pairs of dated rasters with CVAT, Label Studio and labelme, TiTiler chips in the middle, GeoJSON out
- [Copernicus Marine Layers](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/copernicus-marine/): How the Copernicus Marine Service serves its ocean layers as tiles, the four overlays the basemap library carries, and how to add any other one by hand
- [Coverage Footprints](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/coverage-footprints/): Where the coverage overlays' footprints come from, and how the 3D and LiDAR ones are built
- [Custom Protocols](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/custom-protocols/): What a MapLibre custom protocol is, every scheme this app registers, and the registry that lets every consumer reach every one of them
- [Dataset indexes and release-hosted assets](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/dataset-indexes/): The elevation datasets the library streams from other people's buckets, the index each one needs (an upstream VRT, a VRT built here and kept on a GitHub release, a small committed ledger, or none), their resolution, extent and size, how to open the same indexes in QGIS or GDAL, and the releases that hold what the repository does not
- [Derived Terrain Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/demdiff-protocol/): demdiff:// — subtracting one elevation source from another, tile by tile, and the alpha-254 convention that keeps holes flat
- [Making the demo videos](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/demo-videos/): How the demo videos are made by agents — takes recorded with agent-browser and a DevTools screencast, cut in Remotion with Remocn components, and the commands that run the pipeline
- [Draping custom layers](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/draping/): What MapLibre drapes over its terrain and what it does not, why Matcap and Phong have a raster path and a live GL path, and the tile-seam fix
- [Equations & Formulas](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/equations/): The exact math behind every terrain-derivative visualization mode
- [Esri Wayback viewer on a map: every World Imagery release since 2014, side by side](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/esri-wayback/): Browse Esri World Imagery Wayback on a free interactive map: every release since February 2014 on a timeline, two dates side by side with a swipe, next to Google Earth historical imagery and Google Earth Timelapse. Then how the releases, their capture dates and the service at wayback.maptiles.arcgis.com work
- [Fumadocs integration](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/fumadocs-customization/): How this documentation site uses Fumadocs — the visual editor (Studio), the added components and generators, and the Next base-path fixes
- [NASA G-LiHT](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/g-liht/): What glihtdata.gsfc.nasa.gov and LP DAAC serve, what the KMZ pictures encode (elevation, not hillshade), the gliht:// reader, the CORS proxy, the Earthdata route and the 1 521-campaign catalog
- [Google Earth Historical (Time Machine) Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/ge-historical/): How the gehist:// protocol reverse-engineers Google Earth's historical imagery, and how it's wired into this app
- [Google Earth Timelapse on a map: every year from 1984 to 2022](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/google-timelapse/): Watch Google Earth Timelapse year by year on a free interactive map, in the browser: 39 cloud-free mosaics of the whole Earth, 1984 to 2022, next to Esri Wayback and Google Earth imagery. Then how the gtimelapse:// protocol reads the tiles and how Google builds them
- [Indexing, SEO and Agents](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/indexing-and-seo/): What each discovery file and tag does, and how to register the site with Google and Bing
- [MapLibre layer blend modes: what they could do for Terrain Viewer](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/layer-blend-modes/): MapLibre GL JS 6.18 blends a raster, fill or line layer with the map under it (multiply, screen, overlay, color, luminosity, plus-lighter). One section per place the viewer could use it, and what it cannot replace: the overlay split's wipe and its difference mode.
- [Layer Order and Slots](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/layer-order/): Why every layer is inserted beforeId an invisible placeholder, and the order those placeholders are in
- [ArcGIS LERC Elevation Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/lerc-protocol/): lerc:// — decoding Esri's float raster codec into Terrarium tiles, and why the tile pyramid is the only anonymous way into an ArcGIS elevation service
- [Lighting Effects (Matcap / Phong / Hard Shadows)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/lighting-effects/): Why these use a real surface normal and a live-GL fast path instead of the pseudo-elevation trick
- [LRM (Local Relief Model)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/lrm/): Why LRM needs a genuinely different pipeline than slope/curvature/etc
- [Map Bounds and Underzoom](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/map-bounds-and-underzoom/): Fencing the camera to a dataset's footprint without making the dataset impossible to see — maplibre-xy's Underzoom, the 1-degree floor, and the footprints that crash constrain
- [Non-Geo Relief Visualization](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/non-geo-relief-visualization/): Preparing non-georeferenced DSM/RGB data (frescoes, artifact scans) as web-ready COGs
- [On-the-fly Mosaics, titiler-cmr and Planetary Computer](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/on-the-fly-mosaics/): How the NASA HLS pill composites granules through NASA VEDA's titiler-cmr, how the Planetary Computer catalogs tile a STAC search over Landsat and Sentinel-2 through the pcmosaic:// protocol, and how a Maxar, Vantor or NOAA capture is drawn from its COGs through capture://
- [Tile Performance and Workers](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/performance/): What a tile costs in each visualization mode, what the background workers buy, how many threads a page uses, and how the speed-up of November 2026 was obtained
- [Post-Crisis Response](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/post-crisis-response/): Who produces terrain and imagery right after an earthquake, a landslide, an eruption or a flood, and where that data shows up in Terrain Viewer
- [Product Tour (Coachmark)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/product-tour/): How the walkthrough drives the real app — step preparation, the state snapshot, the spotlight-dismiss problem, and what the coachmark library does and does not give you
- [QGIS Plugin (plan)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/qgis-plugin/): A QGIS plugin with the app's sidebar, in two steps - a panel that writes tile service layers, then the modes computed in Python with numpy - and Send2MapApp, the app's "Open in" list in QGIS.
- [Quantized Mesh Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/quantized-mesh-protocol/): quantized-mesh:// — rasterising Cesium's terrain TINs into Terrarium tiles, the geographic-to-Mercator tile mapping, and why the meshing libraries do not help
- [GitHub releases, what each one holds](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/releases/): The GitHub releases of Iconem/terrain-viewer are a file store as much as a version list - desktop installers, the docs screenshots, slide deck PDFs, demo screencasts, UX flow captures and dataset indexes each have their own tag. What each holds, who writes it, who reads it, and how to add or retake a file
- [Search performance, what the reports say](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/search-performance/): Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster readings for terrain-viewer.iconem.com and historical-satellite.iconem.com, dated - which queries and pages bring people, where the reach is, what does not work, and what was changed in the site because of it
- [Setup](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/setup/): Running the app, its structure, and its architecture
- [One Source Schema](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/source-schema/): Built-in terrain sources, library entries and your own sources are one record type, looked up by id in one place and resolved by one function.
- [STAC search internals](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/stac-search/): How the STAC search tab talks to APIs, static catalogs and the federation, why it uses no STAC client library, and what a stac-geoparquet reader would add
- [State reference (URL & storage)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/state/): Every URL parameter the app reads, generated from the source at build time — state parameters mirrored by nuqs, instruction parameters read once on load, and the settings kept in localStorage
- [Tech Stack](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/tech-stack/): The libraries and services this app is built on
- [Terrain Analysis Rendering Pipeline](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/terrain-analysis-pipeline/): How Slope, Aspect, Curvature and friends turn a raster-dem source into a colored layer
- [Tile Caches](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/tile-caches/): The two caches every custom protocol sits on, and the ArrayBuffer detachment rule that governs both
- [Tile service (Scalar)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/tile-service/): What the app draws, served as XYZ tiles and as pictures of a viewport over HTTP, from a Docker image; its addresses and parameters browsed with Scalar
- [Upstream requests](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/upstream-requests/): Feature requests to the libraries and services Terrain Viewer builds on, drafted here before they are posted, with their status and our workaround meanwhile
- [URL as an API (Scalar)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/url-api/): The viewer's URL described as an OpenAPI document, browsed with Scalar — every parameter with the right control for its type
- [UX flows](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/ux-flows/): The /ux-flows page, a map of the app's screens and the flows a user walks through them, with a real screenshot on every screen - its three views, how the screens are captured by agent-browser, and how to add a screen or a flow
- [PMTiles and COG Contours](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/vendored-protocols/): The two protocols this app registers but does not compute — a third-party archive reader and a worker-backed contour generator
- [VRT Mosaic Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/vrt-protocol/): vrt:// — reading a GDAL VRT mosaic in the browser, reprojecting it with proj4, and the two ways it refuses a tile rather than stalling
- [WMS Float32 DEM Protocol](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/wms-float32-protocol/): Bridging a plain WMS elevation service into MapLibre's raster-dem pipeline
- [WMTS sources](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/dev/wmts/): Reading a WMTS GetCapabilities document and turning a layer into a MapLibre tile template: matrix set check, matrix names, dimensions, STAC links, CORS

## Features

- [Desktop App (Electrobun)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/desktop/): The web app packaged as a desktop application with Electrobun - what the build produces, what launcher.exe and cottontail.exe are, the portable (no installer) path, icons, docs and fullscreen
- [Frescoes & Artifact Scans](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/frescoes-and-artifacts/): Using the relief-visualization toolkit on non-georeferenced photogrammetry — wall paintings, reliefs, small finds
- [Open In](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/open-in/): Hand the current viewport off to other web map viewers — River-REM, Search-EO, ESRI Wayback, Google Earth/Maps, Bing Maps 3D, BBBike, ShadeMap, LiDAR Lens, or your own URL template
- [Projects (Import / Export)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/projects/): Bundling sources, bookmarks, drawings, settings, and view state into a portable file — plus ?project= URL presets
- [Settings](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/settings/): The Settings dialog — appearance, caching, storage, beta features, API keys, map bounds and project presets
- [Streaming & Storage Settings](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/advanced/streaming-settings/): COG streaming engine, elevation quantization precision, client-side export, tile caching, and browser storage persistence
- [Use with AI Assistants](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/ai-assistants/): A skill and an llms.txt that let ChatGPT, Claude and coding agents open Terrain Viewer on any place and visualization
- [API keys: where to get each one, and what it unlocks](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/api-keys/): Every key Terrain Viewer accepts in Settings, API Keys: Mapbox, MapTiler, HERE, Planet, Cesium ion, Google and the Copernicus Sentinel Hub instance id. What each unlocks, the page where you create it, and how the app keeps it out of links and builds.
- [Auto source detection](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/auto-source-detection/): Paste any URL in Add Terrain or Add Basemap and the dialog finds its type - tile templates, WMS, ArcGIS, COG, VRT, PMTiles, TileJSON, STAC, Allmaps and IIIF - from the URL itself, then from the response headers and first bytes
- [Basemaps and Overlays](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/basemaps/): Satellite basemaps, overlays, a basemap per view, and Remove paper for scanned maps
- [Bookmarks](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/bookmarks/): Saving and organizing views
- [Bring Your Own Data (BYOD)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/byod/): Adding your own terrain/basemap sources, including local files
- [Catalog search](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/catalog-search/): Finding data you have no URL for, from the Add Terrain and Add Basemap dialogs - STAC catalogs and APIs, NextGIS QMS and the OSM Editor Layer Index - and the app's own sources published as STAC
- [Coverage Map of LiDAR, DEM and Imagery Sources](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/coverage-overlays/): See on the map where each elevation or imagery source has data before switching to it: national LiDAR footprints, DEM tiles, 3D coverage, historical imagery footprints, with the sources covering any point you hover.
- [Demo videos](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/demo-videos/): The narrated demo of Terrain Viewer and the raw screencast takes it was cut from, recorded by agents from the production site, served from the demo-takes release
- [Embedding / iframe](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/embedding/): Everything the app shows is in its URL — how to compose a link or an iframe that loads your own COGs and vector data, the parameters that are instructions rather than state, and the project JSON preset format
- [Export & Share](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/export-and-share/): Snapshots, DEM GeoTIFF and contour exports, historical batch export, and social sharing
- [Historical Imagery Timeline](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/historical-imagery/): The historical imagery mode, its timeline panel, the Catalogs picker, a tick's card and the dedicated entry point
- [Historical Sources](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/historical-sources/): Every historical source the timeline can show, by provider and by catalog, and which archives can or cannot be added
- [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/keyboard-shortcuts/): Every global keyboard shortcut, in one place
- [MCP Server](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/mcp-server/): Ask Claude or another assistant for a place in plain words and get the Terrain Viewer view in the conversation, through a server it can call
- [National LiDAR and DEM Data by Country, Free Elevation Services](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/national-datasets/): Free elevation data from national mapping agencies, country by country, LiDAR DTM and DSM at 0.5 m to 30 m (France, the Netherlands, Spain, the UK, the USA, Canada, Japan and fifty more), viewed in the browser as terrain, no download.
- [National Open-Data Terrain (tablecn)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/national-datasets-tablecn/): The national, regional, surface-model and global terrain datasets of the library as one tablecn data table in client mode, for a side-by-side comparison with the National Open-Data Terrain page
- [nDSM and DEM Difference: compare two elevation models](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/ndsm-and-comparison/): Subtract a DTM from a DSM for a normalised digital surface model (building and tree heights), or two dates for elevation change, in the browser from any two sources, with the offset auto-aligned.
- [River-REM](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/river-rem/): Iconem's companion app for river-relative elevation models, and how this app hands off to it
- [Slide decks](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/slide-decks/): Five presentations of Terrain Viewer, live with a presenter view, and as PDFs, built from the open-slide decks in the repository
- [Split & Compare Modes](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/split-modes/): Off, Overlay, and Side — comparing terrain/basemap sources against each other
- [Sun Position](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/sun-position/): The astronomy behind the app's light direction, shadow calculator, and the standalone sun estimator
- [Global DEM Tile Sources and Basemaps: Mapterhorn, Mapbox, MapTiler, AWS, Esri](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/terrain-sources/): The worldwide elevation tile sources behind the viewer (Mapterhorn, Mapbox Terrain-RGB, MapTiler, AWS Terrarium, Esri World Elevation LERC), their resolution and licences, and the satellite and map basemaps.
- [Tools](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/tools/): Drawing, Elevation Picker, the Sun and Shadow Calculator, Image Georeferencer and Animation
- [Terrain Visualization Modes: hillshade, slope, aspect, curvature, sky-view factor, relief models](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/visualization-modes/): Each visualization mode of the free terrain viewer, with a picture: hillshade and multidirectional lighting, slope, aspect, curvature, sky-view factor, local relief model, contours, hypsometric tint, and how to combine them.
- [Visualization Modes Description](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/visualization-modes-description/): Not a standalone page — single source of truth embedded into the Visualization Modes docs page and the app's own Settings dialog
- [Walkthrough](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/features/walkthrough/): Every step of the in-app guided tour (Coachmark) — intro, Terrain deep dive, Historical Imagery deep dive

## Resources

- [Compared with Other Tools](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/compared-with-other-tools/): Where Terrain Viewer fits next to RVT, QGIS, Google Earth, Cesium, OpenTopography, GeoLibre, forge3d and the rest, and when each is the better choice
- [Credits & Inspiration](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/credits/): Who built this, related projects, and what it's inspired by
- [Topography, Geomorphometry, Hydrology](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/geomorphometry/): Scientific literature and tools behind the terrain-analysis modes
- [MapLibre GL Features](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/maplibre/): MapLibre GL JS issues, PRs, and plugins this app builds on or tracks
- [Related Work](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/related-work/): Datasets, viewers and papers close to Terrain Viewer (MERRA-2, ShadeMap, Mapricot shadows, LiDAR Lens, CutSheetRX, Aguacero, OpenGlobus), what each is and why it matters here, with a comparison of shadow techniques and the open status of the Petén lidar surveys
- [Research References](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/research-references/): Studies from earthquake geology, volcanology, glaciology, rivers, ecology, landscape archaeology and heritage monitoring that read the ground from elevation data and historical imagery, each linked to its area in Terrain Viewer, with the methods and datasets behind the app's modes
- [Research References Table](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/research-references-table/): All of Terrain Viewer's research references as sortable, filterable tables by section, by field, year, whether a study opens in the app, has a free copy or an elevation change, and whether it cites RVT or the Copernicus DEM
- [Research References Table (tablecn)](https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/docs/resources/research-references-tablecn/): Terrain Viewer's research references as one tablecn data table in client mode, the same data as the Research References Table, for a side-by-side comparison of the two table implementations
